label: Robert J. Kaminski
narrative: Robert Kaminski is the one witness in the Malmstrom cluster who was close to the hardware rather than to the story, and his account is in direct and checkable tension with the Air Force's own paper. He is described as a Boeing engineer on the team sent to Malmstrom after the Echo Flight shutdown. In a 1997 letter to researcher Jim Klotz he wrote that the investigation team found nothing that would explain ten missiles dropping off alert, no significant failures and no engineering data that accounted for it, and that the inquiry was ordered ended mid-stream with no report to be filed. The first half of that is corroborated by the 341st Strategic Missile Wing history, which records in the engineering report's own words that the teams at Malmstrom were unable to determine a logical cause. The second half is contradicted by the same history, which records the investigation continuing at the contractor's facility through 1967, Boeing bench tests in its Network Resolution Area reproducing the fault signature, and three engineering change proposals submitted by Boeing as a result. Both cannot be wholly right, and the board records the tension rather than resolving it, because one of them is a document and the other is a letter thirty years after the fact.
